answer: Like a dawn survey that maps the sky before anyone trades, the network grants rights only for audited useful work: each identity must complete a capped quota of verifiable tasks, such as checking transactions or labeling data, before it can mine or vote. A rotating panel of peers re-checks a sample, like tracking a comet across independent telescopes, and results are published in an atlas of completed work. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking hundreds of audited work histories at once costs far more time and effort than any reward, and a caught cheat loses its quota and faces a cooldown.
